literal: Shedding without ceasing, tears dried up, the collyrium-painted eyes, escaping unable, inescapable affliction in my eyes having placed.
translation: My collyrium-painted eyes, having run completely dry of tears from endless weeping, have now left an inescapable, incurable affliction within me.
modern: தொடர்ந்து அழுது அழுது கண்ணீர் வற்றிப்போன என் மை தீட்டிய கண்கள், தப்பிக்கவே முடியாத தீராத துன்பத்தை என்னிடத்தில் நிலைநிறுத்திவிட்டன.
explanation: In this couplet, the heroine laments the state of her eyes during separation from her lover. Her eyes wept so continuously that they have completely run out of tears ('நீருலந்த'). Having exhausted their ability to weep, these very eyes have now left her with an inescapable, incurable disease of love-sickness ('உய்வில்நோய்') inside her. The word 'உண்கண்' refers to eyes adorned with collyrium, highlighting their former beauty which is now ruined by endless grief.
